name: Test fluids, chemicals and proppant
summary: A fracturing job depends on sand of the right size and strength, chemicals that perform as specified, and water that does not break down the fluid system. The laboratory receives samples of frac sand from transload terminals and suppliers, batches of friction reducer, gel and other chemicals from suppliers or the company's blending plant, and water samples from producers, and tests them against specifications: sieve analysis, shape, turbidity and crush tests for sand, certificate checks and property and performance tests for chemicals, and analysis and compatibility tests for water. Results go back to supply chain and the frac design engineers. The work is slowed by samples that arrive without lot or railcar details, by a queue behind urgent cement tests, and by out-of-spec results that need a retest, a supervisor's decision and a conversation with the supplier or a change to the fluid design.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company running about 16 cementing units from Alberta and northeast BC district bases with bulk blending plants, plus a Calgary cement and fluids laboratory and engineering office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB cementing service lines in 2019-2022: dispatch board and phone, ERP inventory, tablet field tickets, lab database and spreadsheets, cement placement software; no automated blending recipe download or live job data streaming to the office as standard.

unit_of_work: one quality sample (a sand lot or railcar sample, a chemical batch or a water sample)
trigger: A sample arrives at the lab from a sand supplier or transload terminal, the chemical blending plant or a supplier, or a producer's water source, with a request for quality testing.
end_state: Test results are issued to the requester and the retained sample filed; or an out-of-spec lot is rejected and the supplier and supply chain are notified, or the frac design is changed.

volume.seasonality: Follows fracturing activity: highest from October to March as winter programs are designed and sand is stockpiled; lowest during spring break-up.

evidence.note: Kept the organisation file's 150 samples a month. Proppant volume was about 1.34 million tonnes a year (src3), roughly 110,000 tonnes a month; suppliers sample every 9,000 kg under ISO 13503-2 (src6), so the company lab checks only a sample per supplier lot or a few railcars, plus water and chemical samples.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak and pre-season sand stockpiling (November to mid-March)

evidence.note: Estimate tied to the winter fracturing peak described in the organisation file.
About 2.5 to 3 hands-on hours a sample over 150 samples a month (about 3 FTE at 130 productive hours); estimate.
Assigning work, out-of-spec decisions and report sign-off; estimate.
Assesses fluid design changes for incompatible water or off-spec chemicals; not listed for this process in the organisation file; estimate.

systems.name: Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)

resources.name: Friction flow loop and HPHT rheometer for fracturing fluid tests

steps.name: Receive and log the sample
steps.description: A laboratory technologist unpacks the sample, checks the label against the request (supplier, lot or railcar number, product, mesh size or water source), photographs it and logs it in the lab database with a sample number.

error.defect_description: Sample logged against the wrong lot or railcar

next.condition: lot, railcar or product details missing

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Chase the sender for missing details
steps.description: The technologist emails or phones the logistics coordinator, terminal or producer for the missing lot or railcar number, certificate of analysis or water source location.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for the sender's reply
steps.description: The sender looks up the shipment in the railcar tracking portal, the supplier's paperwork or its field records and replies, sometimes only after a reminder.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Prioritise and assign tests
steps.description: The lab supervisor sets the priority against urgent cement and frac design work, chooses the test set for the sample type and specification, and assigns it to a technologist in the work list.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Split and reduce the proppant sample
steps.description: The technologist reduces the bulk sample with a sample reducer and splitter to test portions, and seals a retained portion with the sample number for storage.

evidence.note: Sample reduction and splitting procedures and retained samples (src6); times are estimates.

steps.name: Run sieve analysis
steps.description: The technologist weighs a test portion onto a stack of calibrated sieves, shakes it on the sieve shaker, weighs what is retained on each sieve and calculates the share within the designated mesh range.

control.basis: ISO 13503-2 test procedures agreed between the company and its sand suppliers

evidence.note: Sieve analysis is section 6 of ISO 13503-2 (src6); times are estimates.

steps.name: Test shape, turbidity and acid solubility
steps.description: The technologist estimates sphericity and roundness under the microscope against the standard chart, measures turbidity of a washed portion, and runs acid solubility when the specification calls for it.

next.condition: crush test required (new source or periodic check)

evidence.note: Sphericity and roundness, acid solubility and turbidity are sections 7-9 of ISO 13503-2 (src6); share needing crush tests is an estimate.

steps.name: Run crush-resistance test
steps.description: The technologist loads a sieved portion into the crush cell, applies the stress level for the product class in the load frame, then sieves out and weighs the fines generated.

evidence.note: Crush-resistance test is section 11 of ISO 13503-2 (src6); times are estimates.

steps.name: Analyse the water sample
steps.description: The technologist measures pH, specific gravity, chlorides, hardness, iron, sulphate and bacteria on the producer's water sample, comparing it with the limits for the planned fluid system.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Run fluid compatibility tests
steps.description: The technologist mixes the water with the planned friction reducer or gel and crosslinker at field loadings, runs the friction loop or rheometer test and checks for scale or precipitates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check the certificate of analysis
steps.description: The technologist compares the supplier's or blending plant's certificate of analysis for the chemical batch with the product specification: active content, specific gravity, pH and appearance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Measure chemical properties
steps.description: The technologist measures specific gravity, pH and viscosity of the batch and compares them with the certificate and the previous batches.

next.condition: performance test required (new product or supplier)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Run chemical performance test
steps.description: For a new product, a new supplier or a periodic check, the technologist tests performance in a standard water, for example friction reduction in the flow loop or crosslink and break time for a gel.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Compare results with the specification
steps.description: The technologist enters all results in the lab database, compares them with the specification and with the supplier's certificate, and flags any value outside limits.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Retest the retained portion
steps.description: The technologist repeats the failed test on a fresh split from the retained portion to rule out a sampling or test error before the result is reported.

evidence.note: Material for further testing is split from the retained sample (src6); share confirmed is an estimate.

steps.name: Decide what to do with the out-of-spec lot
steps.description: The lab supervisor reviews the confirmed result with supply chain and decides whether to reject the lot, accept it with a deviation for less critical stages, or ask frac engineering whether the design can use it.

next.condition: assess a design change or deviation

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Notify supplier and supply chain
steps.description: The lab supervisor sends the results to the supplier and the logistics or procurement coordinator, asks for the lot to be held or replaced, and records the non-conformance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Assess a design change
steps.description: A frac design engineer reviews the out-of-spec water or chemical result, decides whether chemical loadings, friction reducer type or proppant mesh can change, and records the decision for the affected pads.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for the supplier's response
steps.description: The supplier reviews its own test records and retained sample for the lot and agrees to replace it, credits it or disputes the result.

evidence.note: Suppliers keep test records for at least a year and retained samples for six months (src6); response time is an estimate.

steps.name: Review and sign the result
steps.description: The lab supervisor checks that the right tests were run, the values match the instrument records and the pass or fail call is right, then signs the result in the lab database.

control.basis: Company laboratory quality procedure: supervisor sign-off of quality results

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Issue result and file the retained sample
steps.description: The technologist emails the signed result to the requester and the frac design engineers, updates the supplier quality tracker and stores the retained sample with its number.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Sample details missing
exceptions.description: No lot, railcar or product details, so the lab chases the sender.

exceptions.name: Out of specification confirmed, lot rejected
exceptions.description: The retest confirms the failure and the supplier is asked to replace or credit the lot.

exceptions.name: Out of specification, design change
exceptions.description: Frac engineering changes the fluid design or accepts a deviation.

exceptions.name: Passes on retest
exceptions.description: The first result was a sampling or test error.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from sample received to result issued

evidence.note: Estimate: most sand and chemical tests take a few hours of bench time but wait in a queue behind urgent cement tests; supplier disputes take longer.

benchmarks.unit: kg of frac proppant per sample, at least

evidence.note: ISO 13503-2 section 4.4.1 (src6).

pain_points.description: Quality samples queue behind urgent cement tests for rigs, so sand and chemical results come back days after the material has been used.

evidence.note: Shared lab and technologists in the organisation file; estimate.

pain_points.description: Samples arrive without lot or railcar details, so results cannot be tied to a shipment until the sender replies.

evidence.note: Typical practice; estimate.

pain_points.description: Field sampling rarely matches the supplier's continuous sampling, so out-of-spec results are disputed.

evidence.note: ISO 13503-2 notes field sampling rarely duplicates continuous sampling and that supplier and customer must agree methods (src6).

sources.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Cementing activity tracks the WCSB rig count (201 rigs in Q4 2022, 176 in Q4 2021); 17 cementing units operated in Q4 2022; annual average of 16 cementing units in the field in 2021 and 2022; cementing about 16-19% of revenue; 1,335,000 tonnes of proppant pumped in 2022 and 1,364,000 in 2021; oilfield cement and proppant sourced from suppliers in Canada and the United States.

sources.title: ISO 13503-2:2006 Petroleum and natural gas industries - Completion fluids and materials - Part 2: Measurement of properties of proppants used in hydraulic fracturing and gravel-packing operations (preview pages)
sources.publisher: International Organization for Standardization (preview hosted by iTeh Standards)
sources.supports: Standard procedures for sampling and testing proppants: sieve analysis, sphericity and roundness, acid solubility, turbidity, bulk and apparent density, crush resistance, loss on ignition of resin-coated proppant. Samples taken from a flowing stream, never a static pile; for frac proppant at least one sample per 9,000 kg, at most 10 samples per bulk container combined; reduction with a sample reducer and splitter; supplier keeps test records at least one year and retained samples of at least 0.25 kg for six months; supplier and customer agree sampling methods.

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs and headcounts are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).
Sample mix is 55% proppant, 25% producer water and 20% chemical batches; the split is an estimate.
Lab instruments that a test ties up (crush press, friction loop) are added as resources the organisation file lacks; counts are estimates.
Results for rejected chemical lots go back to chemical procurement and blending; this link is not in the organisation file's process_map entry.
The design engineer takes part for out-of-spec results but is not listed among the process_map roles.
Water compatibility tests ordered for a specific pad design are counted in the frac treatment design workflow; samples here are routine or producer-submitted checks.
